author: Golden State Today
title: UC Davis admits record 48,015 first-year students for fall 2026
text:
UC Davis admits record 48,015 first-year students for fall 2026
The University of California, Davis, has offered admission to 48,015 applicants for first-year study for fall 2026, a 4.5% increase over last year and a new record high, according to statistics released by the University of California on July 29.
UC Davis also extended offers to 10,138 transfer students, including 9,456 from California Community Colleges. Both figures represent increases from the previous fall. The university received a total of 122,271 applications for fall 2026—a rise of 1.8% over last year's record—and included a record number of California residents.
The university expects approximately 6,300 new first-year students this fall, with about 73% coming from California. Among admitted transfer students, UC Davis anticipates enrolling around 3,100, with roughly 96% being in-state residents. "California residents matriculate at higher rates than U.S. domestic and international students," the statement said. About 83% of UC Davis students enrolled in fall 2025 were California residents—figures consistent with systemwide percentages across the ten-campus University of California system.
Among admitted first-year California resident students for fall entry, approximately one-third (34%) would be the first generation in their families to attend college and more than one-third (36%) are from low-income backgrounds. For transfers from community colleges in the state: about forty-four percent would be first-generation college attendees and half are from low-income backgrounds.
Ethnic breakdowns among those admitted as California first-year students include: African American (3.8%), American Indian (0.5%), Hispanic/Latino(a) (27.6%), Pacific Islander (0.3%), Asian American (43.2%), White (19.4%), and unknown ethnicity (5%). Among U.S. domestic transfers from state community colleges: African American (5%), American Indian (0.8%), Hispanic/Latino(a) (27%), Pacific Islander (0.3%), Asian American (38%), White (26.4%), and unknown ethnicity (2.5%).
Information is subject to change as additional waitlisted candidates may be admitted or admissions conditions verified; final enrollment data will be available January next year.
University of California Davis extends its research and educational efforts globally to address issues such as climate change and food security; it features facilities like the Bodega Marine Laboratory for coastal research; it has achieved top national rankings in agriculture, veterinary medicine and sustainability; it began as an extension focused on agriculture; it serves society through research and public service; Gary May served as chancellor, all according to the official website.
